aboutParagraphs: Aeden Fruits International is a fresh fruit supply and cold chain logistics company headquartered in Panangad, Kochi, Kerala, with additional offices in Bengaluru, Karnataka, and Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra. The company operates across three business lines: retail partnerships, wholesale supply operations, and cold chain logistics services, reflecting a vertically integrated approach to fresh produce distribution.

The company's product range includes ten fruit varieties presented on its website: berries, oranges, apples, pears, dragon fruit, plums, kiwi fruit, peaches, mandarins, and pomegranates. With offices spanning three major Indian cities, Aeden Fruits is positioned to serve retail and wholesale buyers across South and West India, supported by the cold chain infrastructure needed to move fresh produce between sourcing points and buyers without quality loss.

This case study covers the website design and development work delivered by Teknoppy — the site's structure, its business-line and product presentation, and how multi-location information is organised for a retail or wholesale buyer evaluating a fresh produce supplier. It does not cover Aeden Fruits' sourcing operations, logistics network, or supplier relationships, which are the company's own domain.
challengeLead: Creating an intuitive supplier portal that balances multiple commercial buyer journeys:

challenges.title: Three business lines needed to read as three distinct paths
challenges.description: A retail store owner looking for a stocking partnership and a distributor looking for bulk wholesale supply are asking different questions, and folding both into one generic 'services' section made it harder for either to find their path in.

challenges.title: Ten fruit varieties needed individual presentation
challenges.description: A buyer evaluating sourcing options wants to see specific fruit categories clearly, not a single combined product block that treats berries and pomegranates as interchangeable line items.

challenges.title: Three office locations needed clear, findable placement
challenges.description: With operations spanning Kochi, Bengaluru, and Navi Mumbai, a prospective buyer needed an easy way to identify which office serves their region rather than a single generic contact page.

challenges.title: Cold chain capability is a genuine differentiator that wasn't standing out
challenges.description: For fresh produce, cold chain logistics is often the deciding factor in a supplier relationship, so it needed to be presented as a core capability rather than a line item buried among other services.

challenges.title: Careers and blog content were competing with core buyer content
challenges.description: Job-seekers and readers browsing blog posts have different intent from a retail or wholesale buyer researching a supply partnership, so these needed their own space rather than crowding the pages a buyer actually needs.

objectiveLead: Teknoppy was engaged to design and build a website that lets a retail or wholesale buyer understand Aeden Fruits' product range, business lines, and location coverage, and reach out with confidence. The brief centred on:
objectives: Structuring retail partnerships, wholesale supply, and cold chain logistics as three distinct, findable business lines
Presenting the ten-variety fruit range with individual product profiles rather than one combined catalogue block
Making the Kochi, Bengaluru, and Navi Mumbai office locations easy to identify and match to a buyer's region
Giving cold chain logistics visible standing as a core capability, not a secondary mention
Creating one consistent enquiry path across product pages, business-line pages, and the homepage
approachLead: How Teknoppy built a business-line-first, multi-city architecture:

approachPillars.title: Navigation built around three buyer paths
paragraphs: The site's information architecture separates retail partnerships, wholesale supply, and cold chain logistics into their own clear sections, so a retail store owner and a bulk distributor each land on content built for their specific need rather than a shared generic page.

approachPillars.title: Products presented as individual profiles
paragraphs: Each of the ten fruit varieties — from berries and dragon fruit to pomegranates and kiwi fruit — gets its own clear presentation on the Products section, giving a buyer a real sense of the range rather than a single undifferentiated list.

approachPillars.title: Three locations made easy to match to a buyer's region
paragraphs: The Kochi headquarters, Bengaluru office, and Navi Mumbai office are presented with clear, distinct location detail, so a prospective partner in any of the three regions can quickly identify the relevant point of contact.

approachPillars.title: Cold chain logistics given standing as a core capability
paragraphs: Rather than treating cold chain logistics as a supporting mention, the site presents it as one of the company's three defined business lines, matching how much weight this capability actually carries in a fresh produce buyer's decision.

approachPillars.title: Careers and blog content kept separate from buyer journeys
paragraphs: Careers and blog sections are structured as their own distinct areas of the site, so a retail or wholesale buyer moves straight to supply and product content without that path being cluttered by unrelated content.

approachPillars.title: One enquiry route, repeated
paragraphs: The same enquiry path is repeated consistently across product pages, business-line pages, and the homepage, so a buyer who's ready to make contact doesn't have to hunt for how.

approachPillars.title: Consistent brand and location details site-wide
paragraphs: The company name and contact details for each of the three offices are kept consistent across every page, so the business reads as one coherent, verifiable multi-location supplier rather than a set of loosely connected pages.

whyMattersParagraphs: A fresh produce supply relationship carries real operational weight for a retail or wholesale buyer — product quality, delivery reliability, and cold chain integrity directly affect their own business. That makes clear, specific content about business lines, product range, and location coverage more useful to a prospective partner than broad claims, and it's why the site was built to make that structure visible rather than folded into generic service language.

The same structure supports how AI-driven search and answer engines now handle B2B supplier research. When each business line and product category is described in plain, specific, crawlable text rather than combined into one general page, both traditional search and AI Overviews or assistant-style answers can extract and represent it accurately, which matters as more retail and wholesale buyers start supplier research by asking an AI tool to identify fresh produce suppliers in a given city or region.

Keeping the company name and each office's location detail consistent across every page, and keeping the three business lines and ten product categories clearly separated rather than merged into one catalogue, is what lets search engines resolve Aeden Fruits International as one coherent, multi-location entity and understand each page's specific topic — the foundation for being found for the location-specific and product-specific searches a real buyer actually runs.

faqs.question: What business lines does Aeden Fruits International operate?
faqs.answer: Three: retail partnerships, wholesale supply operations, and cold chain logistics services.

faqs.question: Which fruit varieties does Aeden Fruits International supply?
faqs.answer: Ten varieties are presented on the website: berries, oranges, apples, pears, dragon fruit, plums, kiwi fruit, peaches, mandarins, and pomegranates.

faqs.question: Where are Aeden Fruits International's offices located?
faqs.answer: The company is headquartered in Panangad, Kochi, Kerala, with additional offices in Bengaluru, Karnataka, and Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra.

faqs.question: Does Aeden Fruits International offer cold chain logistics?
faqs.answer: Yes — cold chain logistics is one of the company's three core business lines, alongside retail partnerships and wholesale supply.

faqs.question: Can a retail store become a stocking partner with Aeden Fruits International?
faqs.answer: Yes — retail partnerships are a dedicated business line, structured separately from the company's wholesale supply operations.

faqs.question: Does Aeden Fruits International supply wholesale buyers and distributors?
faqs.answer: Yes — wholesale supply operations are presented as a distinct business line from retail partnerships, for buyers sourcing at larger volumes.

faqs.question: How do I contact Aeden Fruits International about a supply partnership?
faqs.answer: An enquiry path is available consistently across the website's product pages, business-line pages, and homepage, so you can reach out from whichever page brought you there.

faqs.question: Does Aeden Fruits International have career openings?
faqs.answer: Yes — the website maintains a dedicated Careers section, kept separate from the product and business-line content.
